messages:
dina: Heads-up — POC customer wants a Private deployment with on-prem egress via their firewall. They prefer PrivateLink but their netops is asking about TLS inspection, SNI preservation, and whether we can preserve client src IPs. Handing to @sam @maria for network + pricing details.

sam: Who's the contact on the customer side? Do they need client IP preserved end-to-end, or just consistent static egress IPs? Those are different patterns.

dina: Contact is Claire (netops). She said: 'we need static egress for allowlisting and we'd like to keep client IP if possible for our logs.' Also asked about MTU and any ports beyond 443.

maria: Quick summary: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) = isolation + no routing across VPCs; VPC peering/TGW = routing but broader access. For typical private deploys we recommend PrivateLink when customers want tight control and per-account allowlists.

maria: Note on src IP: PrivateLink by design terminates the connection at our endpoint ENI. The TCP source on our side will be the connector instance NAT, so you will see our egress IPs, not the original client IP. If they must see original client IP, options are:
- run a customer-facing proxy in their VPC that forwards X-Forwarded-For to your logs (app-layer)
- maintain an on-prem proxy that preserves src via GRE/VXLAN and terminates TLS inside their network (complex)
- we can discuss a custom connector that supports client IP preservation but that adds ops/security overhead and isn't standard.

sam: For allowlist + firewall the minimal ask is: allow outbound to our egress IPs (we'll provide a short list) on 443. If PrivateLink, also allow the interface endpoint ENI CIDRs for health checks and DNS. If peering/TGW, open the relevant CIDR ranges.

devon: Security checklist items from my side:
- Provide FQDNs and static IPs for allowlist (we need both if their firewall does FQDN + TLS inspect).
- Will the customer do TLS inspection? If yes, we need to review risk: TLS MITM breaks certificate pinning for some workloads and can break webhook/federated auth flows.
- mTLS: do they require mutual TLS to our endpoints? If so, we need to scope certs and rollover policy.

dina: They WILL do TLS inspection and asked whether SNI passthrough is supported.

devon: SNI passthrough: if they inspect TLS, the firewall usually terminates TLS and reissues a cert. That will change the TLS identity the client sees unless the firewall re-signs with a customer-trusted CA. For services that verify cert chains or use pinning, this will break. We recommend: avoid TLS inspection for traffic to Redwood endpoints OR use an app-layer proxy that preserves the original SSL/TLS session semantics.

dina: Claire also asked for a sample firewall snippet that she can share with her ops team.

maria: Sample (customer firewall egress allowlist) — replace <EGRESS_IPS> with the 1–3 addresses we'll provide during handoff:

```
# Allow HTTPS to Redwood Private deploy egress IPs
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/22 to <EGRESS_IPS> port 443 comment "Redwood private egress"
# DNS for private endpoint resolution (if using AWS Private DNS)
allow udp from 10.0.0.0/22 to 169.254.169.253 port 53 comment "VPC DNS (example)"
# Health and management (if using PrivateLink)
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/22 to <ENDPOINT_ENI_CIDR> port 443 comment "PrivateLink endpoint health"
```

sam: Also call out: if they want BYOIP / preserve egress IPs on their side, they can advertise their own EIPs into the design and we can NAT using those, but that requires a network-runbook and extra billing for EIP usage + data transfer.

maria: Pricing note to share w/ customer: PrivateLink endpoints incur AWS endpoint hourly + data processing fees; Private deployment egress data transfer charges still apply (region dependent). Dedicated (reserved capacity) pricing is different — tends to be better if they have sustained high throughput, but Dedicated is a separate procurement. I'll attach rough deltas in the sales playbook.

devon: For the security questionnaire: I'll need the completed section on network controls, cert management, and incident contact. If they are doing TLS inspection, we should add a question about which CA they use for re-signing and whether they will whitelist our cert pinning exceptions.

deploy-bot: Redwood Private deploy docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/private/connectivity (internal) — includes sample ENI CIDR behavior, how to request egress IPs, and runbook for BYOIP.

dina: Awesome — I'll send Claire the snippet and the docs link. Can someone join a short sync to walk netops through the firewall bits? Friday 10:00am PT works for me. @sam @maria @devon you in?

sam: Yes — put me on for 10.

maria: I'll be there.

devon: Can do. I'll bring the questionnaire checklist.

dina: Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

(End thread)
